title: The Resistance Training Dose Response: Meta-Regressions Exploring the Effects of Weekly Volume and Frequency on Muscle Hypertrophy and Strength Gains
population: 67 studies with 2058 participants (79.1% male, 20.9% female; mean age about 25 years).
key_findings: Sets were classed as direct or indirect for the measured muscle; counting an indirect set as half a set (fractional counting) fitted the data better than counting it as a full set or as zero.
With fractional counting, both hypertrophy and strength increased with weekly volume, with diminishing returns that were considerably more pronounced for strength.
Weekly frequency showed effects on hypertrophy compatible with negligible, while strength increased with frequency, again with diminishing returns.
methods: Multilevel meta-regressions of weekly set volume and weekly frequency against hypertrophy and strength, reported as posterior probabilities, adjusted for intervention duration and training status; three ways of counting indirect sets were compared.
limitations: Comparisons are largely between studies, so they show associations across protocols rather than effects within one person; most participants were young men; the half-set weight for indirect sets is one of three modelled options, chosen by relative fit.

verification.retraction_check: No retraction or correction notice in Crossref updated-by or in the PubMed publication types on 2026-11-25.
